_about: Rules for the classical tests next to the model (R/stat_tests.R, table stat_tests.tsv). The design and the outcome type pick the test (first auto row that matches); assumption checks are reported, not used to switch tests (pre-testing distorts error rates). Biodes may ask for more: analysis.stat_tests = [test ids or families]; analysis.posthoc = {type: pairwise | vs_control | none, control: level, adjust: method}.
_note_sphericity_correction: GG (Greenhouse-Geisser) for every within-subject term with more than two levels; 'girden': Huynh-Feldt when the GG epsilon > girden_threshold (Girden 1992), else GG; 'none'.
_note_adjust: p-value adjustment within each family of comparisons (one family per 'by' level, emmeans default). Holm: valid under any dependence and never less powerful than Bonferroni. vs_control uses dunnettx unless analysis.posthoc.adjust says otherwise.
_note_emmeans_model: within-subject contrasts from the multivariate model: each contrast has its own variance (a paired t-test when there are no between factors), so no sphericity assumption.

families.treatment_effect: main-effect pairs of each treatment factor (averaged over the others); simple effects of the first factor within each level of the second when two treatment factors interact
families.interaction: simple effects: pairs of each goal factor within each level of the other
families.time_course: pairs of time points within each group (within the named group for scope within_group)
families.trend: none: the slope is the test

_note_outlier_iqr: extreme outliers: beyond Q1 - 3 IQR or Q3 + 3 IQR within a cell (rstatix::identify_outliers is.extreme).
_note_default_family: family of the test picked automatically per outcome type; others run when asked (analysis.stat_tests or params outcome = list(stat_tests = ...)).
_note_min_expected: prop_test: when any expected count is below this, Fisher's exact test is run instead (Cochran 1954); this is the validity of the chi-squared approximation, not an assumption pre-test.
_note_skew_report_median: descriptives.tsv 'report' column: median (IQR) when |skewness| > this, else mean (SD).
_note_skew_note: checks: residual (or difference) skewness beyond this is reported with the note that a log10 or square-root scale, or a GLM, may fit better; Bioana does not transform on its own.
_note_mcnemar_exact_max: McNemar: with this many discordant pairs or fewer, the exact binomial p on the discordant pairs is the primary p (the chi-squared approximation is poor).
_note_proportion_ci: descriptives of binary and nominal outcomes: exact (Clopper-Pearson, binom.test) 95% CI per proportion.
_note_expected_ratio: goodness of fit: analysis.expected_ratio = {category: weight} (e.g. {'purple': 3, 'white': 1}); chi-squared against the ratio per treatment group and overall, the exact multinomial test (rstatix::multinom_test) when an expected count < min_expected; Cohen's w = sqrt(chi2 / N).
_note_categorical_block_terms: fixed block terms in binary / ordinal / nominal models with fewer than min_units_per_block units per block: the block coefficients bias the odds ratios away from 1 (Neyman-Scott; pairs double the log OR). binary / ordinal -> a random block intercept (1 | block): glmer / clmm, ORs conditional on the block; nominal (no mixed engine) -> the block is dropped from the multinomial model (marginal ORs) and the generalized CMH test stratifies on it. Simitall check: 150 blocks of 2, true purple log OR 1.10, fixed blocks 2.13.
_note_robust: family robust (WRS2, trimmed means, R/robust.R): run on request (analysis.stat_tests: ["robust"] or an id) and, when robust_when_outliers, next to the primary test whose checks find extreme outliers; the primary test never changes. trim: share trimmed from each tail; seed: bootstrap effect-size CIs.
